setup.zh: 坑底蜷着一只小银狐，伤得很重，只剩一条尾巴，尾根八处断口。它睁眼，龇牙。
setup.en: A little silver fox lies curled in the pit, badly hurt: one tail left, eight clean cuts at its root. It opens its eyes and bares its teeth.

recap.zh: 谷底的浅坑里，你救起一只伤重的小银狐——一条尾巴，尾根八处断口。
recap.en: In a pit on the valley floor you took up a badly hurt little silver fox — one tail, eight cuts at its root.

zh: 坑底一点银光，一明，一暗。
只剩一条尾巴。尾根上，八处断口。
en: A silver light in the pit, bright, then dim.
A little silver fox, fur like moonlit frost.
One tail left. At its root, eight clean cuts.

text.zh: 坑边的泥上没有一个脚印，也没有血拖过的痕迹——它倒像跟你一样，是从上头掉下来的。
text.en: No footprint in the mud at the rim, no trail of blood: it seems to have fallen from above, like you.

text.zh: 八处断口，一处比一处齐，不是野兽咬的，也不是夹子夹的——夹子夹不了这么齐。
text.en: Eight stumps, each cleaner than the last. Not a beast's bite, not a trap — no trap cuts so clean.

story.zh:
他没有走过去，先蹲在一棵银叶树后面看了很久。坑边没有脚印，没有血迹拖过的痕迹，四下里也没有别的动静。他捡起一根枯枝扔到坑边，那光还是一明一暗，并不理会。他这才一点一点地挪了过去。

坑里是一只狐狸。很小，比吴婆婆家那只猫还小一圈——吴婆婆家那只猫胖得像个枕头，这只狐狸大概只有半个枕头。

它蜷在坑底的泥水里，一身的毛是银色的，不是灰，是真正的银，像月光冻成了一层霜铺在它身上，雨水落上去，不沾也不湿，就那么滑了下去。可它伤得很重，一条后腿歪着，身上好几道口子，血把银毛染成了暗红。

它身后只有一条尾巴，尾巴根上还有好几处断口，整整齐齐，像给什么极快、极利的东西一刀一刀斩断的。小满数了数，共是八处。

白狐狸，银的，一条尾巴，比猫还小，受了伤，跑不远。

他蹲在坑边，一动不动。崖根底下那堆银叶子，离这里不到半里。他怀里那锭银子硌着心口，沉甸甸的。一锭银子。马三要的鹿皮，十张也换不来一锭。

他愣了很久，把怀里吴婆婆的木牌摸了出来，就着那一点银光，一条一条地数木牌上那只蜷着的小狐狸的尾巴，数来数去，是九条。

便在这时，坑里的狐狸睁开了眼睛。那是一双金色的眼睛，瞳仁竖着，冷得像冬天的井水。它看着他，龇了一下牙，喉咙里发出一声又小又凶的呜咽，可它连头都抬不起来。

他爹说过，受伤的野兽最凶，别碰。
story.en:
He didn't go straight to it. He crouched behind a silver-leafed tree and watched a long time. No footprints at the hollow's edge, no trail of dragged blood, nothing else stirring. He picked up a dead branch and tossed it to the edge; the light went on bright and dim and paid it no mind. Only then did he edge over, bit by bit.

In the hollow was a fox. A very small one, a size smaller than Granny Wu's cat — Granny Wu's cat was fat as a pillow; this fox was maybe half a pillow.

It lay curled in the muddy water at the bottom, its fur silver — not grey, true silver, like moonlight frozen into a layer of frost — and the rain ran off it without wetting it at all. But it was badly hurt: a hind leg twisted, several gashes, blood staining the silver dark red.

Behind it was only one tail, and at the root of that tail were several stumps, clean and even, as though something very fast and very sharp had cut them off one stroke at a time. Xiaoman counted: eight.

A white fox, silver, one tail, smaller than a cat, hurt, can't run far.

He crouched at the edge of the hollow and didn't move. The heap of silver leaves at the foot of the cliff was less than half a li away. The ingot in his jacket pressed against his heart, heavy. One ingot of silver. Ten of the deer hides Ma San wanted wouldn't buy one.

He stayed frozen a long time, then took Granny Wu's token from his jacket, and by that point of silver light counted, one by one, the tails of the little fox curled on it. He counted and counted: nine.

Just then the fox in the hollow opened its eyes. They were golden, with slit pupils, cold as a well in winter. It looked at him and bared its teeth, a small fierce whimper in its throat — but it couldn't even lift its head.

His father had said: a wounded animal is the fiercest; don't touch.

label.en: Take off your jacket and wrap it up

exits.means: saves the fox, picks it up, wraps it in the jacket, helps it

story.zh:
小满看了它很久，心想：它要是死在这儿，就什么都不是了；它要是活下来——不知道它会是什么。可他知道，一只尾巴给人一刀一刀斩掉的东西，和一个给人一把推到灶台边上的孩子，差不太多。和一个拿一锭银子雇进岭来、喊回去又喊不回去的孩子，也差不太多。

他脱下了外衣。那是他娘去年冬天拿他爹的旧袄改的，袖口打着补丁，补丁上还打着补丁。他用枯枝挑着，轻轻盖在它身上，再隔着衣裳把它抱了起来。它还是咬了他一口，隔着两层布，咬在他虎口上，不深，可是很疼。

他「嘶」了一声，却没有松手，说道：「不怕。我也掉下来了。咱俩，做个伴。」

它不咬了。它在他的衣裳里抖了一下，然后把脸埋进了那块补丁里。
story.en:
Xiaoman looked at it a long time and thought: if it dies here, it's nothing at all; if it lives — he didn't know what it would be. But he knew that something whose tails had been cut off one stroke at a time, and a boy who'd been shoved into a stove, weren't so very different. Nor a boy hired into the ridge for one silver ingot, called back and unable to come back.

He took off his jacket — the one his mother had cut down last winter from his father's old padded coat, patches on the cuffs and patches on the patches — lifted it on a stick and laid it gently over the fox, then gathered it up through the cloth. It bit him anyway, through two layers of cloth, in the web of his thumb — not deep, but it hurt.

He hissed, and didn't let go. "Don't be scared. I fell down here too. We'll keep each other company."

It stopped biting. It shivered once inside his jacket, then buried its face in the patch.

exits.means: leaves the fox alone, backs away, walks off

story.zh:
小满往后退了一步，又一步。坑里那点银光，一明，一暗，一明——暗下去的那一下，比刚才长。

他停住了。他想起那八道断口，整整齐齐的，一刀一刀；又想起灶台，想起那只在半空里翻了两个筋斗的碗。他的脚，便再也迈不动了。
story.en:
Xiaoman took a step back, then another. The silver light in the hollow went bright, dim, bright — and the dim lasted longer than before.

He stopped. He thought of those eight stumps, clean and even, one stroke at a time; and of the stove, and the bowl that turned two somersaults in the air. And his feet wouldn't carry him another step.
